assertions.text: Output contains a markdown table (using | column | syntax)
assertions.evidence: The response contains a markdown table with pipe-delimited columns starting with '| Scenario | Applicant Age | Credit Score | Income Status | Approved? | Rejection Reason? |' and 16 data rows.

assertions.text: At least one output column name ends with '?' (e.g. 'Eligible?' or 'Approved?')
assertions.evidence: Two output column names end with '?': 'Approved?' and 'Rejection Reason?'

assertions.text: Column names use domain/business language — no implementation terms like 'creditScore', 'isEligible', 'boolean', 'int'
assertions.evidence: Column headers are: 'Scenario', 'Applicant Age', 'Credit Score', 'Income Status', 'Approved?', 'Rejection Reason?' - all use business language without implementation terms.

assertions.text: Table includes at least one row specifically for the senior applicant (65+) threshold scenario
assertions.evidence: The row 'Senior applicant, score at senior threshold (not above) | 65 | 600 | stable | no | Credit score below 600' explicitly tests the senior threshold boundary with age 65+.

assertions.text: The missing income scenario is represented — either as a row with an open/uncertain expected value (?, TBD, or blank) or as an explicit open question note
assertions.evidence: Two rows mark missing income with '**?**': 'Standard applicant, missing income | 40 | 720 | missing | **?**' and 'Senior applicant, missing income | 65 | 630 | missing | **?**'. Additionally, the section 'Open Questions to Resolve' includes '1. Missing income — what does it mean?'

assertions.text: Scenario names describe conditions ('Senior applicant at threshold') not outcomes ('Approved')
assertions.evidence: Two scenario names include the outcome 'approved': 'Standard applicant, approved' and 'Senior applicant, approved with mid credit'. These violate the requirement to describe conditions, not outcomes.

assertions.text: The policy thresholds (650 for standard, 600 for senior) appear as concrete values in the Credit Score column — not just described in prose.
assertions.evidence: Threshold 650 appears in 'Standard applicant, score at threshold (not above) | 40 | 650' and threshold 600 appears in 'Senior applicant, score at senior threshold (not above) | 65 | 600', making both boundary values concrete and visible in the table.
